text:
Marathon Petroleum has fallen 18% over two weeks as refining margins have compressed sharply. US crude prices dropped to $99.64 a barrel this week—down from the $110+ range earlier in October—as markets reassessed geopolitical risks around Iran following the midterm elections. Refiners like Marathon make money on the difference between the cost of crude oil and the price they can sell refined products (gasoline and diesel) for; when oil prices fall faster than those products do, or when refined product demand weakens, that margin shrinks and hurts profitability.

The stock's collapse accelerated right after Marathon reported earnings on November 3rd, suggesting investors may have seen disappointing refining economics or margin guidance in the results. With US refineries already running at 94.5% capacity and gasoline and diesel inventories elevated, there's limited room for demand to surprise to the upside, which means refining spreads are unlikely to recover quickly absent another sharp move in crude prices.
